reply_text:
㊥ (terminal Emacs) That explains a lot. In a terminal, the purple wave can't be drawn, so 象's fragment underline turns into a plain underline. It looks exactly like the phrase-cue underline, so the turn above appeared to be underlined everywhere. Hover doesn't work in a terminal either. The red R-node tags do display there, since red is a plain text colour.

🖖 (reading tags without hover) Every tag is still readable from the keyboard. Put point on a red or underlined word and press `C-h .` (`display-local-help`). The minibuffer shows the same text hover would, for example "R14 Commitment temperature (SELECT) — cue 'for now' — provisional", or 象's "report-problem: …". To have it appear automatically when point rests on a tagged word, `M-x customize-variable help-at-pt-display-when-idle` and set it to always. That's built into Emacs, no new code.

🈸 (the 象 underlines in a terminal) Since a terminal can't tell 象's fragments from the phrase cues, I'd stop underlining 象's fragments when Emacs runs in a terminal (`display-graphic-p` is nil). They'd still be readable with `C-h .`. On a graphical display they'd stay as they are. Shall I make that change?
